newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE options traded in cylinder deal.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE options traded in cylinder deal.

text.p: A long cylinder using European style FTSE 100 index options and June FTSE futures was the largest deal struck in the UK equity derivatives market by Wednesday afternoon, dealers said.
"This has been a common strategy recently with traders who are worried the stock market is at a high level and may fall but not want to miss out if the market rallies," said one dealer.
Today's deal involved the sale of 3,000 December 4825 calls in Euro-FTSE at 53p and the purchase of 3,000 December 4025 puts at 84p against buyng 540 March futures at 4340.
One reason the number of futures and options contracts traded were different is because the tick size for futures is 25 stg per point compared with 10 stg per point for FTSE options.

The other reason is that the overall position was delta-neutral and the net delta of the options position was 0.45 which means that for small moves in the market the net options position will change by 0.45 for every one point move by the futures.
In practice, the deal will make money -- by June futures expiry -- if the futures move higher but carries no risk of assignment even if the market goes above 4,825.
This is because European style options can only be assigned on expiry day which will be in December.
By 1440 GMT, spot FTSE was up 3.0 at 4347.7 while March futures were up seven points at 4337.
Over in stock options, the biggest deal was a long straddle in airports management group BAA in which 500 April 550 puts and calls were bought at 19p and 16p each.
For a profit at expiry, BAA shares need to either go below 515p or above 585p. The shares added 3-1/2p to 540p.
